statement.p: Evaluate the integral \int_0^{1}\int_y^{1} \sin(x^2)\ dx\,dy by reversing the order of integration.
With order reversed, \int_a^b\int_c^d \sin(x^2)\ dy\,dx, where a = , b = , c = , and d = .

static.solution:
\sin(x^2) has no elementary antiderivative, so we try integrating with respect to y first. The region of integration is shown in the figure below.
Changing the order of integration, we get \int_0^{1}\int_y^{1}\sin(x^2)\ dx\ dy = \int_0^{1}\int_0^x \sin(x^2) \ dy\ dx, which we can easily evaluate: \int_0^{1}\int_0^x \sin(x^2) \ dy\ dx = \int_0^{1} \sin(x^2)\cdot y\bigg|_0^x\ dx = \int_0^{1} \sin(x^2)\cdot x\ dx = \frac12 (-\cos(x^2))\bigg|_0^{1} = \frac12 ( 1 - \cos 1 ).
